title: Sodium intake, mortality, and life expectancy in US adults: a retrospective cohort study stratified by cardiovascular health
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the associations of sodium intake with mortality and life expectancy, stratified by cardiovascular health (CVH) levels. Design/methodology/approach A retrospective cohort study was conducted using NHANES 2007–2014 data linked to mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019, from the National Center for Health Statistics. Sodium intake was measured via 24-h recall, and CVH was assessed by the Life’s Essential 8 score. Weighted Cox models and life table method were used for analysis. Findings During a median follow-up of 8.9 years, 690 total deaths and 198 cardiovascular disease (CVD) deaths occurred. After adjustment for confounders, no significant associations between sodium intake and CVD mortality were observed across CVH strata. In moderate CVH participants, there was a significant inverse association between sodium intake and all-cause mortality (third quartile [Q3] vs first quartile [Q1]: hazard ratio [HR] 0.62, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.39–0.98; fourth quartile [Q4] vs Q1: HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18–0.85). Similar but nonsignificant associations were seen in good CVH participants. Compared with lowest sodium intake, higher sodium intake was generally associated with higher estimated life expectancy among participants with moderate and good CVH, whereas this pattern was not observed among those with poor CVH. Originality/value These findings suggest that the association between sodium intake and mortality may vary across levels of cardiovascular health. Further prospective studies are needed to determine whether cardiovascular health modifies these associations.

claims.text: No significant associations were observed between sodium intake and cardiovascular disease mortality across cardiovascular health strata after adjustment for confounders.
In participants with moderate cardiovascular health, sodium intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality for the third quartile compared to the first quartile (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39–0.98).

In participants with moderate cardiovascular health, sodium intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality for the fourth quartile compared to the first quartile (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18–0.85).
In participants with good cardiovascular health, associations between sodium intake and all-cause mortality were similar to those in moderate cardiovascular health but nonsignificant.
Higher sodium intake compared with lowest sodium intake was generally associated with higher estimated life expectancy among participants with moderate and good cardiovascular health.
The pattern of higher sodium intake associating with higher estimated life expectancy was not observed among participants with poor cardiovascular health.

future_work.text: Further prospective studies are needed to determine whether cardiovascular health modifies associations between sodium intake, mortality, and life expectancy.
